exposure: mode of delivery (cesarean section vs. vaginal delivery)
outcome: Incidence rate of pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (PA-VTE)
cohort: 499 women with PA-VTE identified from a database of 124,228 VTE events in Korea
finding: The incidence rate of pregnancy-associated venous thromboembolism (PA-VTE) increased 3.2 times between 2006-2010 and 2014-2018, with advanced maternal age, cesarean section, multiparity, and multifetal pregnancies identified as risk factors.
mod_finding: PA-VTE/10,000 deliveries occurred more frequently in cesarean section cases compared with vaginal delivery.
